feature: Risk Register (#2993, Feature #1487) -- the real customer-facing Risk Register page in the rebuilt artifacts/portal (/risk-register), wired to GET /api/portal/risk-register, GET /api/portal/policy-decisions, POST /api/portal/risk-register/:rbdId/accept, and GET /api/portal/risk-register/rbd/:rbdId/versions -- see docs/risk-register-contract-pack.md. No fixture module: every row on screen comes from these endpoints.
notes: WHAT THIS COVERS: the real read shapes (risks[]/decisions[] arrays, the two fields this build added to the wire -- WireAcceptance.status and WireRisk.obligation, both real DB columns that existed but were not previously served), the write-once accept guard (409 on an already-accepted row), the 404 on a nonexistent rbdId, and that the per-RBD version-history read answers cleanly even when no version has ever been captured (empty array, not an error).

WHY NO HAPPY-PATH ACCEPT IS DRIVEN HERE: an acceptance is PERMANENT -- the route refuses a second one with 409 -- so a step that successfully accepts a risk would pass exactly once and then poison every subsequent run of this manifest. A real accept WAS proven end-to-end in-session against a locally-built copy of this exact commit (RBD-2026-103, seeded via lib/db/migrations/manual/2026-08-21-portal-v2-risk-register-testbed-seed.sql): 201 with the new status:'active' field present, an immediate second attempt refused 409, then the row was reset via direct SQL back to its seeded pending_signature/Open state so this manifest's own A3/A4 guards stay true on every run. That sequence is deliberately not a manifest step, for the same non-idempotency reason.

NO UI LOGIN FLOW EXISTS YET FOR artifacts/portal -- this is a known, already-documented cross-cutting gap (see test-manifests/chat/support-chat-active-cards.json's own note), not specific to this build. App.tsx's RequireAuth renders an honest 'Sign in required' panel for an unauthenticated visitor; there is no #email/#password form to drive via uiSteps the way the retired portal-v2 manifests do. Auth Core's real Sign-In screen (#2991, Feature #1648) is what closes this -- once it lands, extend this manifest's uiSteps with a real login block (matching other artifacts/portal manifests) ahead of a `goto /risk-register` and the data-testid selectors this build already ships (risk-row-toggle-<id>, risk-accept-name-<id>, risk-accept-statement-<id>, risk-accept-confirm-<id>, risk-accept-sign-<id>, policy-decision-row-<id>). No code change needed on the risk-register side when that happens.

THE UI STEP BELOW THEREFORE ONLY ASSERTS WHAT IS HONESTLY REACHABLE TODAY: the route mounts and RequireAuth's honest empty state renders for an unauthenticated visitor -- same pattern #2519's manifest uses for /support.

SEEDED TEST DATA: the testbed tenant's real register content is seeded demonstration data (lib/db/migrations/manual/2026-08-21-portal-v2-risk-register-testbed-seed.sql, idempotent via ON CONFLICT), not organic assessment output -- the READ path, the SCOPING and the ACCEPT write path it exercises are real. Re-run that file if A1/A2 below drift.
ENV VARS (BuildConsole -> Settings -> Test Environment Variables): DEPLOY_URL, TEST_PORTAL_EMAIL / TEST_PORTAL_PASSWORD.

apiTests.name: SETUP -- log in as the designated testbed portal account; extract the bearer.
A1 -- the customer-scoped register answers 200 with an array.
A2 -- the policy-decisions view of the same table also answers 200 with an array.
A3 -- accepting an already-accepted seeded risk (RBD-2026-104, always signed by the seed) is refused 409, proving the write-once guard, idempotently re-runnable.
A4 -- a nonexistent rbdId 404s exactly like a real risk belonging to another tenant would (no ID-probing signal).
A5 -- a version history read for an RBD with no captured version answers 200 with an empty array, not an error (#1512 surface, no version ever rendered for the seeded rows).

uiSteps.name: UI1 -- an unauthenticated visitor to /risk-register sees the app's own honest sign-in-required panel (no login page exists yet -- see notes), not a crash or a silently-empty register.
